literature.headline_zh: 人腺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人腺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 浓度在 45 w/w% 和 95 w/w% 之间的乙醇在 30 秒内表现出足够的抗 5 型 HAdV 活性,而浓度在 72.5 w/w% 和 77 w/w% 之间则在 60 秒内有效对抗 7 型 HAdV。观察到“U 形”波动模式,其中减少因子在浓度为 70-80% 时下降,然后在 90% 时再次上升。治疗用40%乙醇处理后,TEM图像显示8型HAdV没有重大变化,但在5型HAdV中在病毒颗粒周围观察到有机物;治疗与66%乙醇混合后,两种类型的病毒颗粒均发生聚集。 [10.3390/v18101170]
在分析的样本中,13 个(9.9%)HAdV 检测呈阳性,118 个(90.1%)呈阴性。系统发育分析鉴定了与 HAdV-F4​​1 和 HAdV-B3 相关的变体,揭示了与参考序列相比的遗传差异和不同的聚类模式。 [10.64898/2026.10.19.26365929]
与对照组相比,脑炎/脑病儿童的中位白细胞计数、降钙素原水平和乳酸脱氢酶水平显着升高(P 值 0.011、0.001、<0.001)。此外,75.47%(40/53)的患者需要机械通气,6个月随访时,38.0%(19/50)的幸存者出现闭塞性细支气管炎,显着高于对照组的11.54%(9/78)(P值0.001)。 [10.1186/s12887-026-07747-w]
腺病毒科分类的丰度在几个儿童 BALF 文库中更为突出,而大多数成人 BALF 文库和实验室环境控制中的信号较低或接近背景范围。一些儿科样本显示出 BALF 衍生的 HAdV-B 相关代表性重叠群的广泛覆盖,衣壳蛋白系统发育支持 HAdV-B 相关谱系布局。 [PMCID:PMC13669151]
检测到强大的细胞和体液 免疫应答,但两个中心之间存在一些差异。RSV 疫苗接种的动物在 RSV 攻击感染后,上呼吸道和下呼吸道中的病毒复制明显减少。 [10.1111/jmp.70121]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Ethanol concentrations between 45 w/w% and 95 w/w% showed sufficient activity against HAdV type 5 over a 30 s period, while concentrations between 72.5 w/w% and 77 w/w% were effective against type 7 over a 60 s period. [10.3390/v18101170]

Of the samples analyzed, 13 (9.9%) tested positive for HAdV, while 118 (90.1%) were negative. Phylogenetic analysis identified variants related to HAdV-F41 and HAdV-B3, revealing genetic differences and distinct clustering patterns compared with reference sequences. [10.64898/2026.10.19.26365929]

Children with encephalitis/encephalopathy had significantly higher median leukocyte counts, procalcitonin levels, and lactate dehydrogenase levels compared to controls (P values 0.011, 0.001, <0.001). [10.1186/s12887-026-07747-w]

Adenoviridae-classified abundance was more prominent in several pediatric BALF libraries, whereas signals in most adult BALF libraries and laboratory environmental controls were low or close to the background range. [PMCID:PMC13669151]

Results Time strongly affected total S-specific IFN-γ responses (F(3, 96.6) = 33.16, p = 8 × 10 −15 ) but not median per-peptide responses (F(3, 95.8) = 0.62, p = 0.606), indicating that the decline reflected contraction in the number of epitopes recognized rather than weakening of individual responses; the same dissociation held within both booster groups. [10.3389/fcimb.2026.1947651]

literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. Ethanol concentrations between 45 w/w% and 95 w/w% showed sufficient activity against HAdV type 5 over a 30 s period, while concentrations between 72.5 w/w% and 77 w/w% were effective against type 7 over a 60 s period. papers.title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime—oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Methods Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock‐vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. Results We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV‐vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV‐specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. Conclusion Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi‐center preclinical vaccine studies.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the potential of mucosal immunization strategies for RSV prevention, which could inform future vaccine development and clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime—oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in a dual-center, randomized, blinded trial involving rhesus macaques. The DNA vaccine was administered via electroporation, followed by mucosal adenoviral boosters. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored over time. The results showed robust immune responses and reduced viral replication in vaccinated animals after RSV challenge. However, unexpected immunity in the control group at one site prevented confirmation of the primary endpoint. The study supports the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting for RSV protection but highlights challenges in multi-center preclinical trials. These findings may inform future vaccine development and clinical trials for RSV prevention.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 DNA 引发——口咽腺病毒加强 疫苗接种 策略针对呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的免疫原性和保护功效。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在两个欧洲灵长类研究机构中进行了一项随机、盲法、双中心研究,涉及恒河猴,包括模拟疫苗接种的动物和模仿原发性 RSV 感染诱导的自然免疫的比较组作为对照。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,DNA 引发后的粘膜腺病毒增强可以诱导针对 RSV 的保护性免疫,同时也凸显了多中心临床前 疫苗 研究中的挑战。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为预防 RSV 的粘膜免疫策略的潜力提供了见解,这可以为未来的 疫苗 开发和临床试验提供信息。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 在欧洲两个灵长类研究机构的一项随机、盲法、双中心研究中,我们评估了针对呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的 DNA 引发口咽腺病毒加强 疫苗接种 策略的免疫原性和保护功效。方法 恒河猴通过电穿孔接收 RSV 融合蛋白 (F) DNA 疫苗,然后两次粘膜施用编码相同抗原的重组腺病毒 媒介。模拟接种动物和模拟原发性 RSV 感染诱导的自然免疫的比较组被纳入作为对照。纵向监测全身和粘膜 免疫应答。结果我们检测到了强大的细胞和体液 免疫应答,但两个中心之间存在一些差异。然而,接种 RSV 疫苗的动物在 RSV 攻击感染后,上呼吸道和下呼吸道中的病毒复制明显减少。一个研究中心的对照组出现了意外的 RSV 特异性免疫,导致无法确认预定义的主要终点。结论 我们的结果支持 DNA 引发后粘膜腺病毒增强诱导针对 RSV 的保护性免疫的潜力,同时强调了与多中心临床前 疫苗 研究相关的挑战。

papers.title: In Vitro Evaluation of the Virucidal Activity of Ethanol Against Human Adenoviruses
papers.abstract: Ethanol has variable effectiveness against non-enveloped viruses; however, several reports suggest that it possesses virucidal activity against human adenoviruses (HAdVs). Ethanol concentrations between 45 w/w% and 95 w/w% showed sufficient activity against HAdV type 5 over a 30 s period, while concentration between 72.5 w/w% and 77 w/w% was effective against type 7 over 60 s period. Type 2 and 8 were less susceptible, however. In this study, we investigated the ability of different concentrations of ethanol to inactivate and change the structure of 19 HAdV types across six subgroups, using the virus infectivity titer for evaluation. After 1 min of ethanol treatment, HAdV types 5 and 8 were observed with transmission electron microscopy. The virucidal activity of disinfectant ethanol against HAdVs in subgroups A, B1 (except for type 21), and C was higher than that in subgroups B2, D, E, and F. We observed a ‘U-shaped’ fluctuation pattern where the reduction factor dropped at concentrations of 70–80% and then rose again at 90%. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估乙醇对 人腺病毒 (HAdV) 的杀病毒活性,因为乙醇对无包膜病毒具有不同的功效,并且先前的报告表明它可能对 HAdV 有效。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对乙醇针对 6 个亚组的 19 种 HAdV 类型的杀病毒活性进行体外评估,使用病毒感染滴度进行评估。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员针对 5、7、8 和 21 型 HAdV 测试了不同浓度的乙醇(45-95 w/w%),使用 传播 电子显微镜 (TEM) 观察结构变化和病毒感染滴度,以评估灭活情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 浓度在 45 w/w% 和 95 w/w% 之间的乙醇在 30 秒内表现出足够的抗 5 型 HAdV 活性,而浓度在 72.5 w/w% 和 77 w/w% 之间则在 60 秒内有效对抗 7 型 HAdV。观察到“U 形”波动模式,其中减少因子在浓度为 70-80% 时下降,然后在 90% 时再次上升。治疗用40%乙醇处理后,TEM图像显示8型HAdV没有重大变化,但在5型HAdV中在病毒颗粒周围观察到有机物;治疗与66%乙醇混合后,两种类型的病毒颗粒均发生聚集。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,轴区域重复次数较少的 HAdV 可能表现出较高的乙醇抗性,这是将结构特征与杀病毒敏感性联系起来的新观察。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果提供了关于乙醇作为消毒剂对抗特定 HAdV 类型的有效性的重要见解,这可以为医疗机构中制定更有针对性的消毒方案提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外条件,可能无法完全反映现实世界的情况,并且证据基于针对一组特定 HAdV 类型的单一研究,因此可信度中等。

papers.title: Adenovirus as a Causative Agent of an Acute Gastroenteritis Outbreak in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil.
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a cause of childhood morbidity and may be associated with human adenovirus (HAdV) infection. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence of HAdV in fecal samples from children with AGE in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, as well as to molecularly characterize the identified strains and evaluate their cytopathic effects in cell culture. Methods A total of 131 samples were analyzed using the nested polymerase chain reaction (Nested-PCR) technique. Molecular characterization was performed through Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, while Vero cell cultures were used to investigate the occurrence of cytopathic effects. Results Of the samples analyzed, 13 (9.9%) tested positive for HAdV, while 118 (90.1%) were negative. The highest detection frequency was observed in children aged three years or younger, particularly those under one year of age. Phylogenetic analysis identified variants related to HAdV-F41 and HAdV-B3, revealing genetic differences and distinct clustering patterns compared with reference sequences. In cell culture, cytopathic effects were observed four days after inoculation, although further analyses are required to confirm productive viral replication. Conclusion These findings demonstrate the presence of HAdV in the samples studied and contribute to understanding its genetic diversity and circulation in Salvador, highlighting the importance of epidemiological surveillance and further studies on its role in the etiology of childhood AGE.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查巴西巴伊亚州萨尔瓦多急性胃肠炎 (AGE) 儿童粪便样本中 HAdV 的发生情况,并对已识别菌株进行分子特征分析并评估其在细胞培养中的细胞病变效应。急性胃肠炎是儿童发病的一个原因,可能与 人腺病毒 感染有关。

elements_zh.methods: 使用巢式聚合酶链式反应 (Nested-PCR) 技术对总共 131 个样品进行了分析。通过桑格测序和系统发育分析进行分子表征,同时使用 Vero 细胞培养物研究细胞病变效应的发生。
elements_zh.main_results: 在分析的样本中,13 个(9.9%)HAdV 检测呈阳性,118 个(90.1%)呈阴性。系统发育分析鉴定了与 HAdV-F4​​1 和 HAdV-B3 相关的变体,揭示了与参考序列相比的遗传差异和不同的聚类模式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现证明了所研究的样本中存在 HAdV,并有助于了解其遗传多样性和在萨尔瓦多的传播,强调了流行病学 监测 以及进一步研究其在儿童 AGE 病因学中的作用的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明需要在儿科人群中进行有针对性的 HAdV 流行病学 监测,并强调进一步研究以阐明其在儿童急性胃肠炎病因学中的作用的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖于单一检测方法,并且缺乏进一步分析来确认细胞培养物中有效的病毒复制。由于该研究的观察性质以及可能存在未解释的混杂因素,证据是中等的。

papers.title: T-cell recognition of SARS-CoV-2 antigen peptides following booster vaccination with mRNA and viral-vectored COVID-19 vaccines
papers.abstract: Background Durability and breadth of SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell responses following booster vaccination remain key to guiding next-generation vaccine design, especially in the context of waning antibodies, emerging variants, and diverse immunological backgrounds. This longitudinal study assessed IFN-γ-producing T-cell responses in 46 fully vaccinated adults who received a booster dose of either the BNT162b2 (mRNA) or Ad26.COV2.S (adenoviral vector) vaccine. All participants were nucleocapsid-seropositive at baseline, with antibody levels stable throughout follow-up, indicating prior natural infection and no incident infection during the study period. Methods Using an ex vivo IFN-γ ELISpot assay, responses were measured at four timepoints (baseline, Months 3, 6 and 9) against spike (S; n = 46) and nucleocapsid (N; n = 16) peptides selected by NetMHCpan-4.1 prediction from overlapping 15-mer libraries spanning both proteins. Each peptide was tested individually, allowing every response to be assigned to a defined sequence. Longitudinal change was modelled using linear mixed-effects models, comparing total with median per-peptide responses to distinguish loss of specificities from loss of per-epitope strength. Analyses were stratified by booster type and vaccination strategy (homologous vs. Results Time strongly affected total S-specific IFN-γ responses (F(3, 96.6) = 33.16, p = 8 × 10 −15 ) but not median per-peptide responses (F(3, 95.8) = 0.62, p = 0.606), indicating that the decline reflected contraction in the number of epitopes recognized rather than weakening of individual responses; the same dissociation held within both booster groups. Ad26.COV2.S boosting was associated with broader S-specific epitope recognition and greater durability, with a subset of responses persisting through Month 9, whereas BNT162b2 recipients showed higher cumulative IFN-γ magnitude through Month 6 — a difference already present before boosting (p = 0.012). N-specific responses declined despite stable anti-nucleocapsid antibody, although two N-derived regions (YGANKDGIIW, VTPSGTWLTY) were recognized at every timepoint. Discussion/conclusions Booster platform and vaccination strategy shaped the magnitude, breadth and durability of SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell responses, with the longitudinal decline appearing to be driven predominantly by narrowing of epitope breadth among Month 3-reactive peptides rather than reduced per-epitope function. The persistently immunogenic S and N epitopes identified here warrant further evaluation as candidates for multi-epitope T-cell vaccine design.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the durability and breadth of SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell responses following booster vaccination with either mRNA (BNT162b2) or adenoviral vector (Ad26.COV2.S) vaccines. The research aimed to understand how different booster platforms influence T-cell immunity, particularly in the context of waning antibody levels and emerging variants. The study followed 46 fully vaccinated adults with stable nucleocapsid antibodies, measuring IFN-γ-producing T-cell responses at four timepoints using an ex vivo ELISpot assay. Results showed that while total S-specific IFN-γ responses declined over time, median per-peptide responses remained stable, suggesting a narrowing of epitope recognition rather than a loss of per-epitope strength. Ad26.COV2.S boosting was linked to broader and more durable S-specific epitope recognition, whereas BNT162b2 recipients had higher IFN-γ magnitude through Month 6. These findings highlight the importance of vaccine platform choice in shaping T-cell immunity and suggest potential candidates for multi-epitope vaccine design. The study's evidence is moderate in strength, as it does not explicitly report limitations in its design.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and half-year outcomes of 53 children with severe adenovirus pneumonia complicated with encephalitis or encephalopathy
papers.abstract: The clinical characteristics and prognosis of children with human adenovirus pneumonia complicated with encephalitis/encephalopathy remain unclear. Clinical data of 53 children admitted to the Respiratory Department of Children’s Hospital o f Chongqing Medical University in 2019 with severe adenovirus pneumonia and complicated with encephalitis/encephalopathy were retrospectively analyzed, 78 cases without encephalitis/encephalopathy were selected as controls. Among the 53 children, 32 (60.4%) were males, with a median age of 18.0 (7.5–37.0) months. All of them had fever and cough, the median fever duration was 12.0 (9.5–15.0) days, and 90.6% (48/53) had listlessness, 62.3% (33/53) had dysphoria, 47.2% (25/53) had hypersomnia, 13.2% (7/53) had seizure. The median leukocyte count, procalcitonin and lactate dehydrogenase of children with encephalitis/encephalopathy were 7.39 (3.53–10.73)*10^9/L, 1.885 (0.390–4.555) ng/ml, and 980.50 (516.40–1938.00) U/L, these were significant differences compared with the control group ( P values were 0.011, 0.001, <0.001), while nasopharyngeal adenovirus load showed no difference. Children with encephalitis/encephalopathy were more likely to be complicated with leukopenia, hypoproteinemia, liver function impairment, coagulopathy, anemia. 75.47% (40/53) children needed mechanical ventilation, and the rate of tracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation time were significantly increased compared with the control group ( P values were 0.039, <0.001). The rates of using gamma globulin, albumin and blood transfusion were 92.45% (49/53), 52.83% (28/53) and 26.42% (14/53) respectively. 94.3% (50/53) children survived and follow-up at half a year later, 38.0% (19/50) showed bronchiolitis obliterans, which was significantly higher than 11.54% (9/78) in the control group ( P value 0.001), and no obvious neurological sequelae were observed. Encephalitis/encephalopathy should be considered in children with severe adenovirus pneumonia in the presence of altered mental status. The clinical manifestations of these children are severe and even life-threatening. Survivors exhibited generally favourable neurological outcomes, however, the incidence of bronchiolitis obliterans was relatively high at six-month follow-up, regular follow-up and active intervention are needed for these patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and half-year outcomes of children with severe adenovirus pneumonia complicated with encephalitis or encephalopathy, as the clinical manifestations and prognosis of such cases remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted on clinical data of 53 children with severe adenovirus pneumonia and encephalitis/encephalopathy admitted to the Respiratory Department of Children’s Hospital of Chongqing Medical University in 2019. These were compared with 78 control cases without encephalitis/encephalopathy.
analysis.methods: The study involved analyzing clinical data, including demographic information, symptoms, laboratory findings, and treatment outcomes. The control group was selected based on similar admission criteria but without the complication of encephalitis/encephalopathy.
analysis.main_results: Children with encephalitis/encephalopathy had significantly higher median leukocyte counts, procalcitonin levels, and lactate dehydrogenase levels compared to controls (P values 0.011, 0.001, <0.001). Additionally, 75.47% (40/53) required mechanical ventilation, and 38.0% (19/50) of survivors developed bronchiolitis obliterans at six-month follow-up, which was significantly higher than 11.54% (9/78) in the control group (P value 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the severity of adenovirus pneumonia complicated by encephalitis/encephalopathy, with notable differences in clinical parameters and outcomes compared to non-complicated cases. The high incidence of bronchiolitis obliterans in survivors suggests a need for long-term monitoring.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical insights into the clinical management of children with severe adenovirus pneumonia and neurological complications, emphasizing the importance of early recognition and targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias. However, the clear statistical differences in key outcomes and the large sample size provide moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the clinical characteristics and half-year outcomes of 53 children with severe adenovirus pneumonia complicated by encephalitis or encephalopathy. The research highlights the severity of these cases, with significant differences in laboratory markers and treatment requirements compared to 78 control patients without neurological complications. The results show that 75.47% of the cases required mechanical ventilation, and 38.0% of survivors developed bronchiolitis obliterans at six-month follow-up, which was significantly higher than in controls. The study underscores the need for early recognition of neurological complications in adenovirus pneumonia and emphasizes the importance of long-term monitoring for affected children. While the retrospective design introduces potential biases, the clear statistical differences and large sample size support moderate confidence in the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨重症腺病毒肺炎并发脑炎或脑病患儿的临床特征和半年转归,因为此类病例的临床表现和预后尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2019年重庆医科大学附属儿童医院呼吸科收治的53例重症腺病毒肺炎合并脑炎/脑病患儿的临床资料进行回顾性分析,并与78例无脑炎/脑病的对照病例进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及分析临床数据,包括人口统计信息、症状、实验室检查结果和 治疗 结果。根据相似的入院标准选择对照组,但没有脑炎/脑病并发症。
elements_zh.main_results: 与对照组相比,脑炎/脑病儿童的中位白细胞计数、降钙素原水平和乳酸脱氢酶水平显着升高(P 值 0.011、0.001、<0.001)。此外,75.47%(40/53)的患者需要机械通气,6个月随访时,38.0%(19/50)的幸存者出现闭塞性细支气管炎,显着高于对照组的11.54%(9/78)(P值0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了腺病毒肺炎并发脑炎/脑病的严重性,与非复杂病例相比,临床参数和结果存在显着差异。幸存者闭塞性细支气管炎的高 发病率 表明需要长期监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为患有严重腺病毒肺炎和神经系统并发症的儿童的临床管理提供了重要的见解,强调了早期识别和有针对性的干预措施的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的选择偏倚而受到限制。然而,关键结果的明显统计差异和大样本量为研究结果提供了适度的信心。

papers.abstract_zh: 人腺病毒肺炎合并脑炎/脑病患儿的临床特征和预后尚不清楚。回顾性分析2019年重庆医科大学附属儿童医院呼吸科收治的53例重症腺病毒肺炎并发脑炎/脑病患儿的临床资料,另选取78例无脑炎/脑病患儿作为对照。53 名儿童中,32 名(60.4%)为男性,中位年龄为 18.0(7.5-37.0)个月。所有患者均有发热和咳嗽症状,中位发热时间为12.0(9.5~15.0)天,90.6%(48/53)有精神萎靡,62.3%(33/53)有烦躁不安,47.2%(25/53)有嗜睡,13.2%(7/53)有癫痫发作。脑炎/脑病患儿白细胞计数、降钙素原、乳酸脱氢酶中位数分别为7.39(3.53~10.73)*10^9/L、1.885(0.390~4.555)ng/ml、980.50(516.40~1938.00)U/L,与正常儿童相比差异有统计学意义。与对照组(P值分别为0.011、0.001、<0.001),而鼻咽腺病毒载量无差异。脑炎/脑病患儿更易并发白细胞减少、低蛋白血症、肝功能损害、凝血功能障碍、贫血。75.47%(40/53)患儿需要机械通气,且气管插管率和机械通气时间均较对照组显着增加(P值为0.039,<0.001)。丙种球蛋白、白蛋白和输血的使用率分别为92.45%(49/53)、52.83%(28/53)和26.42%(14/53)。94.3%(50/53)患儿存活,半年后随访,38.0%(19/50)出现闭塞性细支气管炎,显着高于对照组的11.54%(9/78)(P值0.001),且未见明显神经系统后遗症。患有严重腺病毒肺炎的儿童如果出现精神状态改变,应考虑脑炎/脑病。这些孩子的临床表现很严重,甚至危及生命。幸存者表现出普遍良好的神经学结局,但闭塞性细支气管炎的发病率在6个月随访时相对较高,需要对这些患者进行定期随访和积极干预。
papers.summary_zh: 人腺病毒肺炎合并脑炎/脑病患儿的临床特征和预后尚不清楚。回顾性分析2019年重庆医科大学附属儿童医院呼吸科收治的53例重症腺病毒肺炎并发脑炎/脑病患儿的临床资料,另选取78例无脑炎/脑病患儿作为对照。53 名儿童中,32 名(60.4%)为男性,中位年龄为 18.0(7.5-37.0)个月。所有患者均有发热和咳嗽症状,中位发热时间为12.0(9.5~15.0)天,90.6%(48/53)有精神萎靡,62.3%(33/53)有烦躁不安,47.2%(25/53)有嗜睡,13.2%(7/53)有癫痫发作。脑炎/脑病患儿白细胞计数、降钙素原、乳酸脱氢酶中位数分别为7.39(3.53~10.73)*10^9/L、1.885(0.390~4.555)ng/ml、980.50(516.40~1938.00)U/L,与正常儿童相比差异有统计学意义。与对照组(P值分别为0.011、0.001、<0.001),而鼻咽腺病毒载量无差异。脑炎/脑病患儿更易并发白细胞减少、低蛋白血症、肝功能损害、凝血功能障碍、贫血。75.47%(40/53)患儿需要机械通气,且气管插管率和机械通气时间均较对照组显着增加(P值为0.039,<0.001)。丙种球蛋白、白蛋白和输血的使用率分别为92.45%(49/53)、52.83%(28/53)和26.42%(14/53)。94.3%(50/53)患儿存活,半年后随访,38.0%(19/50)出现闭塞性细支气管炎,显着高于对照组的11.54%(9/78)(P值0.001),且未见明显神经系统后遗症。患有严重腺病毒肺炎的儿童如果出现精神状态改变,应考虑脑炎/脑病。这些孩子的临床表现很严重,甚至危及生命。幸存者表现出普遍良好的神经学结局,但闭塞性细支气管炎的发病率在6个月随访时相对较高,需要对这些患者进行定期随访和积极干预。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨重症腺病毒肺炎并发脑炎或脑病患儿的临床特征和半年转归,因为此类病例的临床表现和预后尚不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2019年重庆医科大学附属儿童医院呼吸科收治的53例重症腺病毒肺炎合并脑炎/脑病患儿的临床资料进行回顾性分析,并与78例无脑炎/脑病的对照病例进行比较。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究涉及分析临床数据,包括人口统计信息、症状、实验室检查结果和 治疗 结果。根据相似的入院标准选择对照组,但没有脑炎/脑病并发症。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与对照组相比,脑炎/脑病儿童的中位白细胞计数、降钙素原水平和乳酸脱氢酶水平显着升高(P 值 0.011、0.001、<0.001)。此外,75.47%(40/53)的患者需要机械通气,6个月随访时,38.0%(19/50)的幸存者出现闭塞性细支气管炎,显着高于对照组的11.54%(9/78)(P值0.001)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了腺病毒肺炎并发脑炎/脑病的严重性,与非复杂病例相比,临床参数和结果存在显着差异。幸存者闭塞性细支气管炎的高 发病率 表明需要长期监测。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为患有严重腺病毒肺炎和神经系统并发症的儿童的临床管理提供了重要的见解,强调了早期识别和有针对性的干预措施的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的选择偏倚而受到限制。然而,关键结果的明显统计差异和大样本量为研究结果提供了适度的信心。

papers.full_text: AbstractHuman adenovirus (HAdV) is an important respiratory virus in children, but sequence-level evidence for HAdV-related signals in lower respiratory tract samples remains limited. In this study, we analyzed metagenomic next-generation sequencing data from 189 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) libraries from pediatric and adult clinical cohorts, including 30 pediatric and 159 adult patients, together with laboratory environmental controls. MEGAN read-level classification was used to screen for Adenoviridae-related signals. HAdV-related contigs were further reviewed, and a BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig was selected for read recruitment and coverage analysis. Phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using penton base, hexon, and fiber protein sequences. Adenoviridae-classified signals were more apparent in pediatric BALF libraries than in adult BALF libraries or environmental controls. Several pediatric BALF libraries showed broad read coverage across the HAdV-B-related representative contig, whereas adult libraries and environmental controls mainly showed low-coverage-breadth signals. Phylogenetic analysis placed BALF-derived penton base, hexon, and fiber sequences within HAdV-B-related lineages. Twenty-seven capsid protein sequences from 12 pediatric samples had best BLASTp matches to references annotated as HAdV-B3 (n = 23) or HAdV-B7 (n = 4). These findings provide sequence evidence for HAdV-B-related sequence signals in clinically selected pediatric BALF samples and support further investigation using targeted assays and genome sequencing.Keywords: bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, HAdV-B, human adenovirus, metagenomic next-generation sequencing, pediatric pneumonia 2.Methods2.1.Sample collection and processingFrom July 2025 to January 2026, a total of 189 residual BALF samples obtained during routine clinical care were included in this observational virome analysis. BALF was obtained during clinical evaluation for suspected pneumonia, although the diagnoses subsequently documented in the available records were heterogeneous. The pediatric cohort comprised 30 BALF samples from the Affiliated Children’s Hospital of Jiangnan University, whereas the adult cohort comprised 159 BALF samples, including 149 from Yixing People’s Hospital and 10 from the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangsu University (Jiangbin Hospital). The pediatric cohort included 29 patients with a recorded pneumonia-related diagnosis and one with acute bronchitis. Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related diagnoses were recorded in 25 of the 30 pediatric patients (83.3%). The adult cohort included 113 patients with pneumonia-related diagnoses and 46 with other recorded clinical conditions. The pediatric and adult cohorts were not designed as clinically matched comparison groups. Detailed sample-level clinical information, cohort summaries, and adult diagnostic subgroup summaries are provided in Supplementary Table S1 (Sheets S1A–S1C).All BALF samples were collected in sterile tubes and transported on dry ice to the biosafety level 2 laboratory at the School of Medicine, Jiangsu University, for subsequent virome analysis. Three laboratory environmental surface controls were included as background references: a PCR instrument surface (Con-P-1), a centrifuge inner surface (Con-L-1), and a biosafety cabinet inner surface (Con-S-1). The three laboratory environmental surface controls were collected using sterile swabs and subsequently subjected to nucleic acid extraction, library preparation, and sequencing using the corresponding virome workflow. For sample processing, frozen BALF samples were thawed on ice. A 600 μL aliquot of each original sample was transferred to a new sterile tube and vortexed for 5 min to ensure sufficient homogenization. The processed samples were then centrifuged at 15,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove cell debris and large particles. The supernatant was collected and stored at −80 °C before viral particle enrichment, filtration, and nucleic acid extraction.2.2.Library preparation and sequencingTo enrich viral particles and reduce the influence of host-derived nucleic acids, 500 μL of preprocessed BALF supernatant was centrifuged at 12,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. The supernatant was then collected and passed through a 0.45 μm pore-size filter to remove residual eukaryotic cells and larger particles. For nuclease treatment, 166.5 μL of filtrate was mixed with 20 μL of 10 × TURBO DNase buffer, 7 μL of TURBO DNase (Invitrogen/Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat. No. AM2238, 2 U/μL; 14 U per reaction), 3 μL of Baseline-ZERO DNase (LGC Biosearch Technologies), 3 μL of Benzonase nuclease (Merck/EMD Millipore, Cat. No. 70664), and 0.5 μL of RNase A, DNase- and protease-free (Thermo Scientific, Cat. No. EN0531, 10 mg/mL). The final reaction volume was 200 μL. The mixture was incubated at 37 °C for 30 min to degrade free nucleic acids that were not protected within viral particles.After nuclease treatment, viral DNA and RNA were extracted using the QIAamp MinElute Virus Spin Kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany; Ref. 57704) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Reverse transcription was included to recover RNA-derived sequences alongside DNA-virus sequences in the same virome workflow. First-strand cDNA was synthesized from the extracted nucleic acids using SuperScript III Reverse Transcriptase (Life Technologies/Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA; Cat. No. 18080-085) and random hexamer primers. The second strand was synthesized using DNA Polymerase I Klenow Fragment (Vazyme Biotech, Nanjing, China; Cat. No. N104-01) to generate double-stranded DNA. Sequencing libraries were then prepared from the resulting double-stranded DNA using the TruePrep DNA Library Prep Kit V2 for Illumina (Vazyme Biotech, Nanjing, China; Cat. No. TD503). A total of 189 BALF sequencing libraries were constructed and sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq 6,000 platform. Sequencing was performed using a 150 bp paired-end strategy with dual-index barcodes for sample demultiplexing.2.3.Bioinformatic preprocessing, assembly, and viral sequence annotationRaw sequencing data were first demultiplexed and paired by the sequencing platform software. Subsequent bioinformatic analyses were performed on a Linux server cluster. Raw reads were quality controlled using Trim Galore v0.6.11 (21) to remove adapter sequences, low-quality bases, and short reads (--phred33 --length 50 --stringency 3 --paired), generating quality-controlled paired-end reads. The quality-controlled reads were mapped to the human reference genome (GCF_000001405.40) using Bowtie2 v2.5.0 (22), and reads mapped to the host genome were removed to obtain host-depleted clean reads.The host-depleted clean reads were subjected to de novo assembly using MEGAHIT v1.2.9 (23) (--min-contig-len 200). The assembled contigs were compared against a local viral protein database using the BLASTx mode of DIAMOND v2.1.18 (24) (-e 1e-5 -k 25 -f 100). The local viral protein database was built from NCBI viral protein sequences and updated in September 2025. The DAA files generated by DIAMOND were then imported into MEGAN v7.1.1 (25) for taxonomic annotation based on the lowest common ancestor (LCA) algorithm.In addition to contig-level analysis, read-level viral classification was also performed. Host-depleted clean reads were compared against the viral protein subset of the NCBI NR database using DIAMOND BLASTx (taxonomy ID 10239; -e 1e-5 -k 25). To reduce false-positive classification caused by non-viral sequences, candidate viral reads from the initial screen were further checked against the complete NR protein database. The retained read-level DIAMOND results were imported into MEGAN and converted into RMA format for subsequent comparative analysis.All 192 libraries were compared in MEGAN v7.1.1 with “Use normalized counts” and “Keep at least 1 read” enabled. Family-level Adenoviridae counts were exported and analyzed in R without further library-size normalization.2.4.Screening of HAdV-related contigs and annotation of the representative contigBased on the MEGAN classification results, contigs annotated as Adenoviridae were further screened. Candidate contigs were manually reviewed using Geneious Prime v2024.0.5. For HAdV-related contigs longer than 500 bp, we focused on whether they contained major capsid genes such as penton base, hexon, and fiber.A near-complete BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig was selected as the reference sequence for subsequent read recruitment analysis. This contig was named JN-BALF-025-35976 and had a length of 35,414 bp. The representative contig contained major capsid genes, including penton base, hexon, and fiber, and its genome organization was annotated in Geneious Prime. Major capsid genes were highlighted in the schematic, while other predicted open reading frames were shown as background ORFs.2.5.Representative contig read recruitment and coverage analysisTo assess read-level support for the assembled HAdV-B-related representative contig, processed paired-end reads from pediatric BALF libraries, adult BALF libraries, and laboratory environmental control libraries were recruited to the representative contig. Host-depleted clean reads were used for clinical BALF samples, while quality-controlled paired-end reads were used for environmental controls. A Bowtie2 index was built from the single representative contig.Read recruitment was performed using Bowtie2 (--very-sensitive-local --no-mixed --no-discordant --no-unal). The alignment results were filtered, sorted, and summarized using Samtools v1.13 (26). Only proper-pair alignment records were retained for downstream analysis (-f 2 -F 3844). Coverage depth was calculated using samtools depth -aa -d 0. Properly paired read pairs were used as the basic counting unit in this study. Two retained proper-pair alignment records were counted as one mapped read pair. The denominator includes all read pairs supplied to recruitment, including both recruited and unrecruited pairs. For each sample, representative-contig RPM was calculated as mapped pairs/input read pairs × 1,000,000 and was used to describe read recruitment abundance. Coverage breadth was calculated as the percentage of bases in the representative contig covered by at least one read and was used to describe the distribution of recruited reads across the contig (Supplementary Table S2).2.6.Extraction of major capsid genes and phylogenetic analysisTo determine the phylogenetic placement of BALF-derived HAdV-related sequences, phylogenetic analyses were performed for three major capsid proteins: penton base, hexon, and fiber. BALF-derived sequences were extracted from HAdV-related contigs, and their target protein regions were confirmed using CDD search (27) and NCBI BLASTp results. Reference sequences were downloaded from the NCBI database and included representative human adenovirus species and major HAdV-B-related types.Multiple sequence alignments were performed using MAFFT v7.526 (28) (--auto) and then trimmed using trimAl v1.5.0 (29) (-automated1). Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using IQ-TREE v2.3.6 (30). The best-fit substitution model was selected automatically by ModelFinder (-m MFP), and major branch support was assessed with 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates (-bb 1,000). The phylogenetic trees were finally visualized using ChiPlot (31) and Adobe Illustrator 2025 v29.0.2.7.Statistical analysis and visualizationAll statistical summaries and graphical visualizations were performed in R v4.3.1 (32). Data processing was mainly conducted using the dplyr, tidyr, readr, and stringr packages. Figures were generated using ggplot2, with scales and patchwork used to optimize axes, legends, and multi-panel layouts. For the descriptive comparison of MEGAN-normalized Adenoviridae abundance between the pediatric and adult BALF groups, a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test was used. Laboratory environmental controls were displayed only as background references and were not included in this statistical comparison. A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1961482/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials 3.Results3.1.MEGAN read classification indicated more prominent Adenoviridae signals in pediatric BALF librariesThe pediatric cohort included 29 patients with a recorded pneumonia-related diagnosis and one with acute bronchitis. Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related diagnoses were recorded in 25 of the 30 pediatric patients (83.3%). The adult cohort included 113 patients with pneumonia-related diagnoses and 46 with other recorded clinical conditions (Supplementary Table S1B). Both cohorts comprised residual clinical BALF samples processed using the same virome workflow, but they differed in sampling center and clinical composition.To obtain an initial read-level assessment of Adenoviridae-related signals in BALF libraries, we compared MEGAN-normalized abundance among pediatric BALF libraries, adult BALF libraries, and laboratory environmental control libraries. Adenoviridae-classified abundance was more prominent in several pediatric BALF libraries, whereas signals in most adult BALF libraries and laboratory environmental controls were low or close to the background range (Figure 1A).Figure 1Read-level Adenoviridae-classified signals in BALF metagenomic libraries. (A) Group-level distribution of MEGAN-normalized Adenoviridae abundance in pediatric BALF libraries, adult BALF libraries, and laboratory environmental control libraries. Each point represents one library. The y-axis shows log10(normalized abundance + 1). The comparison between the pediatric and adult BALF groups was performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Environmental controls were shown only as laboratory background controls and were not included in this statistical comparison. (B) Cohort-wide distribution of Adenoviridae normalized abundance after all libraries were ranked from high to low abundance. Each point represents one library, and colors indicate sample groups. MEGAN-based read classification was used to display read-level classification signals and was not used alone for clinical HAdV infection diagnosis or specific type assignment.Panel A is a box plot showing log10 normalized abundance of Adenoviridae-classified reads among children BALF, adult BALF, and environmental controls. Children BALF display visibly higher and more variable values. Panel B is a scatter plot showing cohort-wide ranking of normalized Adenoviridae abundance, with orange, blue, and green dots representing children BALF, adult BALF, and environmental controls, respectively, highlighting higher values in children.We then ranked all libraries according to their Adenoviridae normalized abundance. Libraries with the highest Adenoviridae abundance were predominantly from the pediatric BALF group, whereas most adult BALF libraries and environmental controls were located in the low-abundance range (Figure 1B). The distribution of Adenoviridae normalized abundance differed between the pediatric and adult BALF groups (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, p < 0.001). Laboratory environmental controls were displayed only as background references and were not included in this statistical comparison. Because the pediatric and adult cohorts differed in clinical composition and sampling center and were not designed as clinically matched groups, this comparison was interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of an independent age effect or age-specific HAdV prevalence. In addition, MEGAN-based classification represents screening-level taxonomic evidence from mNGS data and was therefore not interpreted alone as evidence of clinical HAdV infection or specific HAdV type assignment.3.2.Representative-contig read recruitment showed broader HAdV-B-related read support in pediatric BALF librariesBased on the read classification results, we further used assembled BALF-derived HAdV-related sequences for read-level validation. A near-complete HAdV-B-related representative contig, JN-BALF-025-35976, was selected as the reference sequence. Processed paired-end reads from all clinical and environmental-control libraries were recruited to this representative contig. The representative contig was 35,414 bp in length and contained major capsid genes, including penton base, hexon, and fiber. It was therefore used as a representative assembled sequence for read recruitment analysis (Figure 2A).Figure 2Genome organization and read recruitment features of the BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig. (A), Genome organization of the BALF-derived near-complete HAdV-B-related representative contig. Major capsid genes, including penton base, hexon, and fiber, are highlighted in red. Other genes are shown in green, and predicted ORFs are shown in orange. The horizontal scale indicates nucleotide positions along the 35,414-bp contig, and arrowheads indicate the orientation of annotated features. E and L denote early and late gene regions, respectively. Overlapping features are displayed on separate rows for clarity. (B), Relationship between representative-contig RPM and coverage breadth after read recruitment. RPM represents the number of read pairs recruited to the representative contig per million input read pairs used for recruitment. Coverage breadth represents the percentage of bases in the representative contig covered by at least one read. Each point represents one library, and colors indicate sample groups. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractHuman adenovirus (HAdV) is an important respiratory virus in children, but sequence-level evidence for HAdV-related signals in lower respiratory tract samples remains limited. In this study, we analyzed metagenomic next-generation sequencing data from 189 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) libraries from pediatric and adult clinical cohorts, including 30 pediatric and 159 adult patients, together with laboratory environmental controls. MEGAN read-level classification was used to screen for Adenoviridae-related signals. HAdV-related contigs were further reviewed, and a BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig was selected for read recruitment and coverage analysis. Phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using penton base, hexon, and fiber protein sequences. Adenoviridae-classified signals were more apparent in pediatric BALF libraries than in adult BALF libraries or environmental controls. Several pediatric BALF libraries showed broad read coverage across the HAdV-B-related representative contig, whereas adult libraries and environmental controls mainly showed low-coverage-breadth signals. Phylogenetic analysis placed BALF-derived penton base, hexon, and fiber sequences within HAdV-B-related lineages. Twenty-seven capsid protein sequences from 12 pediatric samples had best BLASTp matches to references annotated as HAdV-B3 (n = 23) or HAdV-B7 (n = 4). These findings provide sequence evidence for HAdV-B-related sequence signals in clinically selected pediatric BALF samples and support further investigation using targeted assays and genome sequencing.Keywords: bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, HAdV-B, human adenovirus, metagenomic next-generation sequencing, pediatric pneumonia
full_text_sections.methods: 2.Methods2.1.Sample collection and processingFrom July 2025 to January 2026, a total of 189 residual BALF samples obtained during routine clinical care were included in this observational virome analysis. BALF was obtained during clinical evaluation for suspected pneumonia, although the diagnoses subsequently documented in the available records were heterogeneous. The pediatric cohort comprised 30 BALF samples from the Affiliated Children’s Hospital of Jiangnan University, whereas the adult cohort comprised 159 BALF samples, including 149 from Yixing People’s Hospital and 10 from the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangsu University (Jiangbin Hospital). The pediatric cohort included 29 patients with a recorded pneumonia-related diagnosis and one with acute bronchitis. Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related diagnoses were recorded in 25 of the 30 pediatric patients (83.3%). The adult cohort included 113 patients with pneumonia-related diagnoses and 46 with other recorded clinical conditions. The pediatric and adult cohorts were not designed as clinically matched comparison groups. Detailed sample-level clinical information, cohort summaries, and adult diagnostic subgroup summaries are provided in Supplementary Table S1 (Sheets S1A–S1C).All BALF samples were collected in sterile tubes and transported on dry ice to the biosafety level 2 laboratory at the School of Medicine, Jiangsu University, for subsequent virome analysis. Three laboratory environmental surface controls were included as background references: a PCR instrument surface (Con-P-1), a centrifuge inner surface (Con-L-1), and a biosafety cabinet inner surface (Con-S-1). The three laboratory environmental surface controls were collected using sterile swabs and subsequently subjected to nucleic acid extraction, library preparation, and sequencing using the corresponding virome workflow. For sample processing, frozen BALF samples were thawed on ice. A 600 μL aliquot of each original sample was transferred to a new sterile tube and vortexed for 5 min to ensure sufficient homogenization. The processed samples were then centrifuged at 15,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove cell debris and large particles. The supernatant was collected and stored at −80 °C before viral particle enrichment, filtration, and nucleic acid extraction.2.2.Library preparation and sequencingTo enrich viral particles and reduce the influence of host-derived nucleic acids, 500 μL of preprocessed BALF supernatant was centrifuged at 12,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. The supernatant was then collected and passed through a 0.45 μm pore-size filter to remove residual eukaryotic cells and larger particles. For nuclease treatment, 166.5 μL of filtrate was mixed with 20 μL of 10 × TURBO DNase buffer, 7 μL of TURBO DNase (Invitrogen/Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat. No. AM2238, 2 U/μL; 14 U per reaction), 3 μL of Baseline-ZERO DNase (LGC Biosearch Technologies), 3 μL of Benzonase nuclease (Merck/EMD Millipore, Cat. No. 70664), and 0.5 μL of RNase A, DNase- and protease-free (Thermo Scientific, Cat. No. EN0531, 10 mg/mL). The final reaction volume was 200 μL. The mixture was incubated at 37 °C for 30 min to degrade free nucleic acids that were not protected within viral particles.After nuclease treatment, viral DNA and RNA were extracted using the QIAamp MinElute Virus Spin Kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany; Ref. 57704) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Reverse transcription was included to recover RNA-derived sequences alongside DNA-virus sequences in the same virome workflow. First-strand cDNA was synthesized from the extracted nucleic acids using SuperScript III Reverse Transcriptase (Life Technologies/Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA; Cat. No. 18080-085) and random hexamer primers. The second strand was synthesized using DNA Polymerase I Klenow Fragment (Vazyme Biotech, Nanjing, China; Cat. No. N104-01) to generate double-stranded DNA. Sequencing libraries were then prepared from the resulting double-stranded DNA using the TruePrep DNA Library Prep Kit V2 for Illumina (Vazyme Biotech, Nanjing, China; Cat. No. TD503). A total of 189 BALF sequencing libraries were constructed and sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq 6,000 platform. Sequencing was performed using a 150 bp paired-end strategy with dual-index barcodes for sample demultiplexing.2.3.Bioinformatic preprocessing, assembly, and viral sequence annotationRaw sequencing data were first demultiplexed and paired by the sequencing platform software. Subsequent bioinformatic analyses were performed on a Linux server cluster. Raw reads were quality controlled using Trim Galore v0.6.11 (21) to remove adapter sequences, low-quality bases, and short reads (--phred33 --length 50 --stringency 3 --paired), generating quality-controlled paired-end reads. The quality-controlled reads were mapped to the human reference genome (GCF_000001405.40) using Bowtie2 v2.5.0 (22), and reads mapped to the host genome were removed to obtain host-depleted clean reads.The host-depleted clean reads were subjected to de novo assembly using MEGAHIT v1.2.9 (23) (--min-contig-len 200). The assembled contigs were compared against a local viral protein database using the BLASTx mode of DIAMOND v2.1.18 (24) (-e 1e-5 -k 25 -f 100). The local viral protein database was built from NCBI viral protein sequences and updated in September 2025. The DAA files generated by DIAMOND were then imported into MEGAN v7.1.1 (25) for taxonomic annotation based on the lowest common ancestor (LCA) algorithm.In addition to contig-level analysis, read-level viral classification was also performed. Host-depleted clean reads were compared against the viral protein subset of the NCBI NR database using DIAMOND BLASTx (taxonomy ID 10239; -e 1e-5 -k 25). To reduce false-positive classification caused by non-viral sequences, candidate viral reads from the initial screen were further checked against the complete NR protein database. The retained read-level DIAMOND results were imported into MEGAN and converted into RMA format for subsequent comparative analysis.All 192 libraries were compared in MEGAN v7.1.1 with “Use normalized counts” and “Keep at least 1 read” enabled. Family-level Adenoviridae counts were exported and analyzed in R without further library-size normalization.2.4.Screening of HAdV-related contigs and annotation of the representative contigBased on the MEGAN classification results, contigs annotated as Adenoviridae were further screened. Candidate contigs were manually reviewed using Geneious Prime v2024.0.5. For HAdV-related contigs longer than 500 bp, we focused on whether they contained major capsid genes such as penton base, hexon, and fiber.A near-complete BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig was selected as the reference sequence for subsequent read recruitment analysis. This contig was named JN-BALF-025-35976 and had a length of 35,414 bp. The representative contig contained major capsid genes, including penton base, hexon, and fiber, and its genome organization was annotated in Geneious Prime. Major capsid genes were highlighted in the schematic, while other predicted open reading frames were shown as background ORFs.2.5.Representative contig read recruitment and coverage analysisTo assess read-level support for the assembled HAdV-B-related representative contig, processed paired-end reads from pediatric BALF libraries, adult BALF libraries, and laboratory environmental control libraries were recruited to the representative contig. Host-depleted clean reads were used for clinical BALF samples, while quality-controlled paired-end reads were used for environmental controls. A Bowtie2 index was built from the single representative contig.Read recruitment was performed using Bowtie2 (--very-sensitive-local --no-mixed --no-discordant --no-unal). The alignment results were filtered, sorted, and summarized using Samtools v1.13 (26). Only proper-pair alignment records were retained for downstream analysis (-f 2 -F 3844). Coverage…
full_text_sections.results: 3.Results3.1.MEGAN read classification indicated more prominent Adenoviridae signals in pediatric BALF librariesThe pediatric cohort included 29 patients with a recorded pneumonia-related diagnosis and one with acute bronchitis. Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related diagnoses were recorded in 25 of the 30 pediatric patients (83.3%). The adult cohort included 113 patients with pneumonia-related diagnoses and 46 with other recorded clinical conditions (Supplementary Table S1B). Both cohorts comprised residual clinical BALF samples processed using the same virome workflow, but they differed in sampling center and clinical composition.To obtain an initial read-level assessment of Adenoviridae-related signals in BALF libraries, we compared MEGAN-normalized abundance among pediatric BALF libraries, adult BALF libraries, and laboratory environmental control libraries. Environmental controls were shown only as laboratory background controls and were not included in this statistical comparison. Coverage breadth represents the percentage of bases in the representative contig covered by at least one read. Each point represents one library, and colors indicate sample groups. Coverage breadth was used to describe the distribution of reads across the representative contig and was not used as a clinical positivity threshold.Panel A shows a genomic map with genes and features annotated by colored arrows, representing their orientation and function. Panel B presents a scatter plot displaying recruitment abundance versus coverage breadth for Children BALF, Adult BALF, and Environmental control groups, with Children BALF having higher coverage. Panel C shows a cohort-wide ranking of coverage breadth, highlighting that Children BALF samples have significantly greater coverage breadth compared to Adult BALF and Environmental control groups.Median coverage breadth was 61.15% (range, 2.31%-100%) in pediatric BALF libraries and 0.796% (range, 0.596%-0.884%) in adult BALF libraries. Coverage breadth in the three environmental controls ranged from 0.788% to 1.194%. full_text_sections.discussion: 4.DiscussionIn this study, we characterized Adenoviridae-related signals in BALF mNGS data from pediatric and adult clinical cohorts. We observed higher Adenoviridae read-classification abundance in several pediatric BALF libraries and then examined these signals using HAdV-related contigs, representative-contig read recruitment, and phylogenetic analyses of penton base, hexon, and fiber. The results support HAdV-B-related sequence signals in a subset of clinically selected pediatric BALF samples, with support from assembly, broad read coverage in several libraries, and phylogenetic placement.HAdV is one of the important viral pathogens associated with respiratory infections and pneumonia in children. Previous studies have shown that HAdV infection can lead to a wide range of clinical manifestations, from mild upper respiratory tract infection to severe pneumonia, and pediatric patients remain a major population of interest in HAdV pneumonia research (33, 34). In pediatric pneumonia or lower respiratory tract infection cohorts in China, HAdV-B3 and HAdV-B7 have frequently been reported as common types (35, 36). Some studies have also shown that HAdV-B7-related infection may present with more severe clinical features than HAdV-B3-related infection (37). The HAdV-B-related mNGS signals identified in pediatric pneumonia BALF in the present study are consistent with previous reports on the epidemiological features of pediatric respiratory HAdV-B. Because the samples in this study were derived from BALF, our findings also suggest that HAdV-B-related signals in lower respiratory tract samples deserve attention in virome studies of pediatric pneumonia.This study further incorporated assembly and read recruitment results to strengthen signal interpretation. mNGS read classification can provide rapid and broad information for pathogen screening, but low-abundance reads, conserved protein regions, and database similarity can all affect taxonomic interpretation (38, 39). In this context, assembled HAdV-related contigs provide longer sequence backgrounds than individual reads. Representative contig read recruitment can further assess whether the assembled sequence is supported by the original sequencing data from the perspective of read distribution. In this study, reads from some pediatric BALF libraries were not only recruited to the HAdV-B-related representative contig, but also covered broad regions of the contig. This finding indicates that HAdV-B-related signals in pediatric BALF had clearer contig-level read support.Coverage breadth was an important interpretive metric in this study. RPM reflects the abundance of recruited reads, but it cannot by itself distinguish whether reads are distributed across the contig or concentrated in a local conserved region. We observed a certain degree of representative-contig RPM signal in adult BALF libraries, but these signals were mainly located in the low-coverage-breadth range. By contrast, several pediatric BALF libraries showed both higher RPM and higher coverage breadth. This difference suggests that HAdV-B-related signals in pediatric samples were more consistent with broad contig support, whereas local recruitment in adult samples was more appropriately interpreted as a low-coverage-breadth mapping signal. This approach reduces the risk of overinterpretation based solely on the number of mapped reads and provides a description that is more suitable for virome data.The pediatric and adult cohorts should not be regarded as clinically matched populations. In addition to age, the two cohorts differed in clinical composition and sampling center. The pediatric cohort was predominantly composed of patients with pneumonia or bronchopneumonia and frequently included recorded respiratory co-pathogens, whereas the adult cohort represented a broader range of clinical conditions. Accordingly, the more prominent HAdV-related signals observed in the pediatric cohort cannot be attributed to age alone and may also reflect differences in underlying disease, co-infection background, clinical indications for BALF sampling, and source population. Nevertheless, representative-contig coverage breadth remained consistently low across the major adult diagnostic categories, and the low-breadth pattern was observed across the adult diagnostic categories summarized in Supplementary Table S1C. We therefore interpret these findings as cohort-level differences in metagenomic signal patterns rather than as estimates of age-specific HAdV prevalence or an independent effect of age.Phylogenetic analysis provided additional lineage information. Molecular typing of HAdV should not rely on a single short fragment. Hexon, penton base, and fiber are major capsid genes commonly used for HAdV typing, and combined analysis of these genes can improve type-related interpretation (40). Sequence variation in the hexon neutralization determinants and fiber knob has also been used for molecular classification of HAdV prototypes (41). In this study, BALF-derived sequences from all three capsid proteins were placed within HAdV-B-related lineages. Best-hit reference annotations were predominantly HAdV-B3, with fewer HAdV-B7 matches, but marker-level matches differed in several samples.HAdV can undergo genetic recombination, and different genomic regions may show discordant evolutionary relationships (42, 43). Recombination, mixed infection, assembly artifacts, and limited discriminatory information in partial protein regions are possible explanations for discordant marker-level matches, but these possibilities cannot be distinguished with the present data. Major capsid-gene sequences can support identification of known HAdV types, whereas whole-genome data are particularly important for characterizing novel types and complex recombinants (16, 40). In this dataset, incomplete marker coverage, discordant reference matches, and the lack of genome-level linkage among markers limited definitive type assignment. We therefore retained HAdV-B-related as the overall lineage description.The available clinical and genomic data were insufficient to assess whether capsid-marker patterns were associated with clinical presentation. Previous studies have reported type-specific differences in pediatric respiratory HAdV infection, including more severe disease associated with HAdV-7 than HAdV-3 in some cohorts (37). However, only a subset of pediatric BALF samples yielded capsid sequences suitable for phylogenetic analysis, several patients had recorded co-pathogens or other associated conditions, and definitive type assignments and standardized clinical outcome data were not available. We therefore present the clinical and genomic information descriptively and do not draw conclusions regarding type-specific disease severity.BALF provided a valuable sampling window for this study. Compared with nasopharyngeal or throat swabs, BALF is closer to the pulmonary lesion site and can provide more direct lower respiratory tract information for pneumonia pathogen analysis. Previous studies have shown that BALF mNGS can improve pathogen spectrum identification in patients with pneumonia and has clinical value in pediatric pneumonia and severe pneumonia (44, 45). The present study was not a clinical diagnostic trial, but a virome analysis based on residual BALF samples. This design allowed us to re-examine the distribution, assembly support, and phylogenetic placement of HAdV-related signals in lower respiratory tract samples. Compared with detecting viral nucleic acids only in nasopharyngeal samples, BALF mNGS can provide more direct sequence evidence for viral signals in the lower respiratory tract of patients with pneumonia.This study also included laboratory environmental surface controls. In virome studies, low-biomass samples, reagent background, and laboratory environmental nucleic acids can affect interpretation of low-abundance viral signals (46, 47). The environmental controls w…
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5.ConclusionThis analysis identified stronger Adenoviridae read-classification signals in pediatric than in adult clinical BALF libraries. Several pediatric samples showed broad coverage of a BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig, and capsid protein phylogenies supported HAdV-B-related lineage placement. These findings provide genomic information from clinically selected lower respiratory tract samples. They do not establish an independent age effect, population prevalence, or type-specific disease severity.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionPneumonia is a common and clinically important lower respiratory tract infection in both children and adults. In practice, the challenge is often not simply to determine whether infection is present, but to interpret pathogen signals accurately in complex clinical samples. The pathogen spectrum of pediatric pneumonia varies with age, season, geographic region, and diagnostic approach, and viruses represent an important component of community-acquired pneumonia requiring hospitalization in children (1). The etiological composition of adult pneumonia is also complex, and clinical interpretation usually requires consideration of sample type, disease severity, and microbiological findings (2). Culture, antigen testing, PCR, and multiplex PCR panels remain important tools in routine pneumonia diagnostics, but these methods usually rely on predefined targets and may not cover all potential pathogens. For pneumonia samples with negative routine tests, discordant results, or complex microbial signals, untargeted sequencing can provide additional information for pathogen profiling.Etiological studies of pediatric pneumonia have shown that viruses are a key pathogen group in lower respiratory tract infections. A study of hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia in the United States reported frequent viral detection and age-related differences in pathogen distribution (3). The PERCH multi-country case-control study also showed that the causes of severe childhood pneumonia are not attributable to a single pathogen group, as viruses, bacteria, and mixed infections may all contribute to disease (4). These findings suggest that pathogen analysis in pediatric pneumonia should not rely solely on conventional bacterial culture, but should also include molecular assays and broader pathogen screening strategies. For virus-associated pneumonia, sample source, detection strategy, and downstream sequence interpretation can all affect the reliability of the results.Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) belong to the genus Mastadenovirus and are non-enveloped, icosahedral viruses with linear double-stranded DNA genomes that replicate in the host-cell nucleus (5, 6). Respiratory disease is commonly associated with HAdV-B, HAdV-C, and HAdV-E, whereas HAdV-D types such as 8 and 37 are associated with epidemic keratoconjunctivitis and HAdV-F40 and HAdV-F41 predominantly cause gastroenteritis (6). Respiratory manifestations include fever, cough, and sore throat and range from upper respiratory tract illness to pneumonia; severe or disseminated infection is of particular concern in immunocompromised patients (5, 6). In murine cells exposed to recombinant HAdV-5 vectors, cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling contributes to IRF3 activation and type I interferon responses (7). These findings provide biological context for HAdV sequence characterization; host pathway activity was not assessed in the present study.HAdV-B-related types have attracted considerable attention in studies of pediatric respiratory infections. Studies of acute respiratory infections in Chinese children have shown that HAdV-B3, HAdV-B7, and some HAdV-C-related types are commonly detected in pediatric respiratory samples (8). A study of pediatric acute respiratory tract infections in Guangzhou from 2010 to 2021 also showed temporal variation in the distribution of HAdV types (9). In pediatric acute respiratory illness cohorts, the composition and clinical features of different HAdV species are not completely consistent (10). Some studies have also suggested that HAdV-7-associated pneumonia may be linked to a more severe clinical course (11). These findings indicate that HAdV-B-related signals in pediatric pneumonia samples deserve further sequence-level characterization.HAdV-related signals are not restricted to pediatric respiratory infections. A study of adults with acute respiratory infection in China detected HAdV-B, HAdV-C, and HAdV-E, suggesting that HAdV-related signals can also be present in adult respiratory samples (12). Including both pediatric and adult BALF cohorts within the same study framework may therefore help describe how HAdV-related signals differ across age-related and clinical sample backgrounds. However, pediatric and adult clinical cohorts may differ in immune status, underlying diseases, pathogen spectrum, and clinical indications for sampling. For this reason, such findings are better interpreted at the level of sample groups and sequencing signals, rather than being simplified into a direct comparison of clinical prevalence.Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) provides an important sample source for analyzing viral signals in the lower respiratory tract. Compared with nasopharyngeal or throat swabs, BALF is closer to the pulmonary lesion site and can more directly reflect microbial and viral nucleic acid signals in the lower respiratory tract. Studies of pediatric lower respiratory tract infections have shown that BALF metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can identify multiple categories of pathogens in complex pulmonary infection samples and can complement conventional diagnostic methods (13). Another study also noted that BALF has long been regarded as an important sample type for detecting lower respiratory tract infections, although its collection is usually limited by clinical indications (14). Virome analysis using residual clinical BALF samples can therefore provide a sequence-level window into lower respiratory tract viral signals without requiring additional invasive sampling.mNGS offers a more open strategy for pathogen profiling in pneumonia samples. Because mNGS does not depend on predefined targets, it can capture nucleic acid signals from bacteria, fungi, viruses, and other microorganisms, making it suitable for pathogen exploration in complex infection samples (7). For virome studies, the value of mNGS lies not only in read-level classification, but also in the ability to combine de novo assembly, read recruitment, and phylogenetic analysis for deeper sequence-level interpretation of candidate viral signals. Molecular typing and phylogenetic placement of HAdV also require sufficient sequence evidence. Traditional HAdV classification once relied on serological methods, but modern HAdV naming and classification increasingly emphasize genome sequences and phylogenetic information (16). Hexon, penton base, and fiber are commonly used major capsid genes for HAdV typing and phylogenetic analysis, as these regions are closely related to antigenicity, cell binding, and viral entry. For HAdV-related fragments assembled from mNGS data, when complete genomes cannot be obtained for all samples, phylogenetic analysis based on multiple major capsid genes can provide a more cautious basis for lineage placement.Several studies have described the molecular epidemiology of pediatric respiratory HAdV across different regions and clinical sample types. Many of these studies focused mainly on nasopharyngeal swabs, throat swabs, or other upper respiratory tract samples, and their core analyses often involved typing and phylogenetic analysis of PCR-positive samples (17, 18). Other studies have explored the utility of BALF mNGS for pathogen detection in pediatric pneumonia or lower respiratory tract infections, suggesting that BALF mNGS can serve as a complementary approach to routine pathogen testing (19, 20). However, virome-level descriptions of HAdV-related signals in BALF from pneumonia patients remain relatively limited. In particular, few studies have integrated read-level classification, assembly-supported contigs, representative contig read recruitment, and phylogenetic analysis of major capsid genes using BALF mNGS data. This gap limits our understanding of the sequence characteristics and phylogenetic background of HAdV-related signals in lower respiratory tract samples.Based on this background, the present study included BALF mNGS libraries from pediatric and adult…

papers.title_original: Viral metagenomic characterization of HAdV-B-related signals in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from pediatric and adult clinical cohorts

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the presence and characteristics of HAdV-related signals in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) from pediatric and adult patients, addressing the limited sequence-level evidence for HAdV in lower respiratory tract samples.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational virome analysis was conducted using 189 residual BALF samples collected from pediatric and adult clinical cohorts between July 2025 and January 2026. The pediatric cohort included 30 samples from the Affiliated Children’s Hospital of Jiangnan University, while the adult cohort comprised 159 samples, with 149 from Yixing People’s Hospital and 10 from the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangsu University (Jiangbin Hospital).
analysis.methods: BALF samples were collected in sterile tubes and transported on dry ice to a biosafety level 2 laboratory for virome analysis. Environmental controls were included as background references, and MEGAN read classification was used to assess Adenoviridae-related signals. The comparison between pediatric and adult BALF groups was performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
analysis.main_results: Adenoviridae-classified abundance was more prominent in several pediatric BALF libraries, whereas signals in most adult BALF libraries and laboratory environmental controls were low or close to the background range. Several pediatric samples showed broad coverage of a BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig, and capsid protein phylogenies supported HAdV-B-related lineage placement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified stronger Adenoviridae read-classification signals in pediatric BALF libraries, suggesting potential differences in viral load or presence between pediatric and adult cohorts. These findings provide genomic information from clinically selected lower respiratory tract samples.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to understanding the genomic presence of HAdV in lower respiratory tract infections, particularly in pediatric populations, which may inform improved diagnostic approaches and surveillance strategies for adenoviral pneumonia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and does not establish an independent age effect, population prevalence, or type-specific disease severity. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on residual samples and the absence of direct clinical diagnosis for HAdV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed viral metagenomic data from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples of pediatric and adult patients to explore HAdV-related signals in lower respiratory tract infections. The research aimed to address the limited sequence-level evidence for HAdV in such samples. Using MEGAN read classification and virome analysis, the study found more prominent Adenoviridae signals in pediatric BALF libraries compared to adult libraries and environmental controls. Several pediatric samples showed broad coverage of a HAdV-B-related contig, and phylogenetic analysis supported HAdV-B lineage placement. These findings provide genomic insights into HAdV presence in clinical respiratory samples but do not establish independent age-related effects or disease severity. The study's observational design and reliance on residual samples limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查儿科和成人患者支气管肺泡灌洗液 (BALF) 中 HAdV 相关信号的存在和特征,解决下呼吸道样本中 HAdV 的有限序列水平证据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2025年7月至2026年1月从儿科和成人临床队列研究收集的189份残留BALF样本进行观察性病毒组分析。儿科队列研究包括江南大学附属儿童医院的30份样本,成人队列研究包括159份样本,其中149份来自宜兴市人民医院,10份来自宜兴市人民医院。江苏大学附属医院(江滨医院)。
elements_zh.methods: BALF 样本收集在无菌管中,并通过干冰运输至生物安全 2 级实验室进行病毒组分析。环境控制作为背景参考,MEGAN 读数分类用于评估腺病毒科相关信号。使用 Wilcoxon 秩和检验对儿童和成人 BALF 组进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 腺病毒科分类的丰度在几个儿童 BALF 文库中更为突出,而大多数成人 BALF 文库和实验室环境控制中的信号较低或接近背景范围。一些儿科样本显示出 BALF 衍生的 HAdV-B 相关代表性重叠群的广泛覆盖,衣壳蛋白系统发育支持 HAdV-B 相关谱系布局。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究在儿科 BALF 文库中发现了更强的腺病毒科读取分类信号,表明儿科和成人 队列研究 之间的病毒载量或存在存在潜在差异。这些发现提供了临床选择的下呼吸道样本的基因组信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于了解下呼吸道感染中 HAdV 基因组的存在,特别是在儿科人群中,这可能为改进 监测 的诊断方法和 监测 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,并未建立独立的年龄效应、人群 患病率 或特定类型疾病的严重程度。由于依赖残留样本且缺乏针对 HAdV 感染的直接临床 诊断,因此证据是中等的。

papers.source_body_en: In this study, we analyzed metagenomic next-generation sequencing data from 189 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) libraries from pediatric and adult clinical cohorts, including 30 pediatric and 159 adult patients, together with laboratory environmental controls. These findings provide sequence evidence for HAdV-B-related sequence signals in clinically selected pediatric BALF samples and support further investigation using targeted assays and genome sequencing.Keywords: bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, HAdV-B, human adenovirus, metagenomic next-generation sequencing, pediatric pneumonia 2.Methods2.1.Sample collection and processingFrom July 2025 to January 2026, a total of 189 residual BALF samples obtained during routine clinical care were included in this observational virome analysis. The retained read-level DIAMOND results were imported into MEGAN and converted into RMA format for subsequent comparative analysis.All 192 libraries were compared in MEGAN v7.1.1 with “Use normalized counts” and “Keep at least 1 read” enabled. Family-level Adenoviridae counts were exported and analyzed in R without further library-size normalization.2.4.Screening of HAdV-related contigs and annotation of the representative contigBased on the MEGAN classification results, contigs annotated as Adenoviridae were further screened. AbstractHuman adenovirus (HAdV) is an important respiratory virus in children, but sequence-level evidence for HAdV-related signals in lower respiratory tract samples remains limited. MEGAN read-level classification was used to screen for Adenoviridae-related signals. HAdV-related contigs were further reviewed, and a BALF-derived HAdV-B-related representative contig was selected for read recruitment and coverage analysis. Phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using...
